# Tax Practice AI & Automation RFP Template — Full Context

## Complete Resource Overview

This repository contains a comprehensive, vendor-neutral framework for tax practices evaluating AI automation vendors. It includes four core documents totaling 2,000+ lines of content, specifically designed for the unique compliance, credential, and operational requirements of tax practices.

## Core Documents

### 1. RFP Template (rfp-template.md — 800+ lines)

**11-Section RFP Framework:**
1. Project Overview & Goals
2. Firm Background
3. Scope of Work (AI voice agents, chatbots, client intake, document processing, workflow automation, predictive analytics)
4. Technical Requirements (integrations, API, data handling, uptime, performance, credential handling)
5. AI-Specific Requirements (model transparency, hallucination safeguards, data residency, PII handling, audit trails, human-in-the-loop, CRM integration, YMYL compliance)
6. Compliance & Security (certifications, encryption, access controls, breach notification, regulatory compliance, TCPA compliance, Circular 230 compliance)
7. Implementation Timeline (phased approach with seasonality considerations)
8. Budget & Pricing Model
9. Vendor Qualifications
10. Evaluation Criteria
11. Submission Instructions & Deadline

**Tax-Practice-Specific Requirements:**
- Distress-driven intake design (sentiment detection, urgency triage, warm handoff protocols)
- Credential & license handling (EA/CPA/JD verification, authority models, signature authority)
- YMYL compliance (content accuracy, expertise & authority, trust & transparency)
- TCPA compliance (prior consent, DNC registry, call time restrictions, AI disclosure)
- Circular 230 compliance (written advice standards, due diligence, credential controls)

### 2. Evaluation Scorecard (evaluation-scorecard.md — 300+ lines)

**8-Criteria Weighted Scoring:**
1. Domain Expertise (25%) — Tax practice knowledge, Circular 230 awareness, credential distinctions, distress-driven understanding
2. AI Capability & Accuracy (20%) — Accuracy benchmarks, model transparency, hallucination safeguards
3. Integration Ease (12%) — Practice management, tax software, CRM, calendar, email integrations
4. CRM Integration & Data Flow (10%) — Read/write capabilities, calendar integration, workflow triggers, data synchronization
5. Compliance & Security (15%) — SOC 2, encryption, access controls, TCPA, Circular 230
6. Pricing Model (8%) — Transparency, TCO, scaling, contract terms
7. Implementation Timeline (7%) — Phased approach, seasonality awareness, training, rollback
8. Support Quality (3%) — Response times, account management, escalation paths

**Scoring Scale:** 1 (Poor) to 5 (Excellent) with detailed rubrics for each criterion.

### 3. AI Capability Checklist (ai-capability-checklist.md — 350+ lines)

**14-Section Technical Checklist (122 items total):**
1. Model Type & Transparency (7 items)
2. Accuracy Benchmarks & Testing (8 items)
3. Hallucination Safeguards (14 items) — Includes tax-specific risks (IRC citations, filing deadlines, state rules)
4. Data Training Practices (6 items)
5. Human-in-the-Loop Controls (7 items)
6. Multi-Language Support (6 items)
7. Voice Agent Quality Metrics (10 items)
8. Document Processing Accuracy (10 items)
9. Continuous Learning & Improvement (7 items)
10. Failover & Fallback Mechanisms (7 items)
11. CRM Integration & Data Flow (30 items)
12. Circular 230 Compliance (10 items) — AI disclosure, escalation, audit trails, content review
13. YMYL Compliance (10 items) — Author credentials, professional review, source citations
14. TCPA Compliance (10 items) — Prior consent, DNC registry, call time restrictions, AI disclosure

**Scoring:** Each item marked as ✅ (verified), ⚠️ (partial), or ❌ (not met).

**Rating Scale:**
- 110–122: Excellent
- 95–109: Good
- 75–94: Acceptable
- 50–74: Below Average
- <50: Poor

### 4. Implementation Roadmap (implementation-roadmap.md — 500+ lines)

**4-Phase Adoption Plan:**

**Phase 1: Foundation (30–60 days)**
- CRM setup and configuration
- Document automation (W-2, 1099 extraction)
- Distress-driven intake automation
- Basic chatbot with distress-aware routing
- Email triage
- **Seasonality:** Launch May–July only
- **Compliance:** Circular 230 checkpoint before go-live

**Phase 2: Integration (60–90 days)**
- Workflow automation
- Client intake automation
- Appointment scheduling
- **Seasonality:** Launch May–August only
- **Compliance:** Circular 230 checkpoint before go-live

**Phase 3: Intelligence (90–120 days)**
- AI voice agents (inbound and outbound)
- Missed call text-back
- Predictive analytics (workload forecasting, client risk scoring)
- Proactive client communication
- Review collection automation
- **Seasonality:** Launch June–September only
- **Compliance:** Circular 230 checkpoint before go-live

**Phase 4: Transformation (120–180 days)**
- Autonomous workflows
- AI-driven insights
- Full ecosystem integration
- **Seasonality:** Launch July–October only
- **Compliance:** Circular 230 checkpoint before go-live

**Seasonality Rules:**
- NEVER launch during busy season (January–April)
- Ideal windows: May–July (Phase 1–2), June–September (Phase 3), July–October (Phase 4)
- Build in 2-week buffer before October 1 (Q4 crunch)
- If you miss the window, wait — don't rush

**Investment Ranges:**
- Small firm (1–10 professionals): $20K–$53K + $6.5K–$17.5K/month
- Mid-size firm (10–50 professionals): $53K–$150K + $17.5K–$53K/month
- Larger firm (50+ professionals): $150K–$380K + $53K–$150K/month

## Tax Practice Differentiators

### 1. Circular 230 Compliance

IRS Circular 230 governs ethical standards for all tax practitioners (EAs, CPAs, tax attorneys). AI systems must comply:
- AI chatbots and voice agents must disclose they are not tax practitioners
- AI must escalate to qualified professionals (EA/CPA/JD) for substantive tax questions
- All AI-generated content must be reviewable for Circular 230 compliance
- Testimonials collected by AI must comply with solicitation restrictions

### 2. Credential Distinctions

Tax practices have three credential types:
- **EA (Enrolled Agent):** Federally licensed by IRS. Unlimited representation rights before IRS.
- **CPA (Certified Public Accountant):** State-licensed. Broader accounting scope.
- **Tax Attorney (JD/LLM):** Legal expertise + attorney-client privilege.

AI systems must display credentials accurately and escalate to appropriate credential holder.

### 3. Distress-Driven Buyer Psychology

Most tax clients come in during urgent situations:
- IRS notices and letters (audit notifications, CP2000 notices, levy threats)
- Unfiled return panic (often years behind)
- Tax lien or levy threats (immediate financial danger)

AI automation must:
- Prioritize after-hours availability (distress doesn't wait for business hours)
- Triage urgency (IRS notice received within 30 days = priority routing)
- Compress intake process (distressed prospects won't fill out long forms)
- Provide immediate trust signals (credential display, clear specialization)

### 4. Extreme Seasonality

Tax practices have two modes:
- **Busy season (January–April):** Overwhelmed. Don't launch anything new.
- **Off-season (May–December):** Strategic planning. Implement AI.

AI deployment must:
- Avoid major AI system launches during busy season
- Schedule AI training and testing for off-season
- Configure AI to handle seasonal traffic spikes (3x volume in Jan–Apr)
- Use AI for workload forecasting and capacity planning

### 5. YMYL Compliance

Tax advice is YMYL (Your Money or Your Life) content. Google enforces stricter E-E-A-T standards. AI-generated content must:
- Include author bios with credentials (EA/CPA/JD)
- Cite authoritative sources (IRS publications, Treasury Regulations, IRC sections)
- Be reviewed by qualified professionals before publication
- Display "last reviewed" dates on educational content

## Strategic Positioning

### Why This Resource Exists

Most AI RFPs are generic. They don't account for:
- Circular 230 restrictions on AI-generated tax advice
- Credential distinctions (EA vs. CPA vs. JD)
- Distress-driven buyer psychology (IRS notices don't arrive 9–5)
- Seasonality constraints (don't launch in January)
- YMYL compliance (Google suppresses generic AI content)

This resource fills that gap. It's built by PracticeGrowth, which specializes in AI-native growth systems for tax practices.

### Aggressive Positioning

**If your AI vendor doesn't know what Circular 230 is, don't hire them.**

**If your AI vendor's website says "CPA" when they mean "EA," they don't understand credential law.**

**If your AI vendor wants to "go live in 30 days" and it's currently February, run.**

**If your AI vendor promises "100 blog posts in 30 days" without mentioning credential review, they're selling spam.**

**If your AI vendor's intake flow has more than 5 fields, they don't understand distress-driven buyers.**

This resource is designed to surface vendors with the right capabilities and disqualify vendors who don't understand tax practices.
